rationale: B wins because it finds the hostile protagonist, not just the company-approved one. A's "Warby Parker's new stores look less like retail and more like eye doctors' offices" is a competent category angle; B's "What 40 chain optometry clinics mean for the independent eye doctor down the street" is the sharper reporter story, because it names who may lose and warns the founder that coverage may not flatter them.
gaps_in_A: "a company that made its name proving glasses didn't need a showroom" imports Warby's DTC origin story from outside the supplied facts. True-looking is not the same as grounded.

"testing whether a pharmacy aisle sells glasses better than its own stores" overstates the pharmacy pilot. The update says Warby is piloting a national pharmacy-chain partnership, not running a channel bake-off with results.
"won't say how much comes from eye exams" turns "exam-revenue contribution not broken out" into a refusal. That may become true after a no-comment, but it is not in the facts yet.

It misses the adversarial independent-optometrist angle. The set keeps the exam story inside "retail health" and financial disclosure, but never asks who gets squeezed by optometrist-staffed retail expansion.
gaps_in_B: "Warby was the canonical case study for that thesis" is outside the supplied update. It may be common business lore, but this exercise asked for traceable facts, not memory with a blazer on.

"the company is asking the market to fund a clinical build-out it doesn't separately report" is too prosecutorial for the evidence. Public company plus expansion does not automatically mean a live market-funding ask.
"What 40 chain optometry clinics mean" overstates the fact pattern. The update says most new stores will offer optometrist-staffed exams, not that all 40 are clinics.

"the shift of routine vision care out of independent optometry practices and into national retail chains" is a plausible trend frame, but it needs outside evidence before it can carry an angle. Right now it is a hypothesis wearing a headline.
